verdict.line: You lose when he lands Death's Grasp and racks up three hits for Darkness Rise mid-trade; you win when your Q-W-E burst drops him before that third hit and you disengage after.

brief.thesis: This lane is decided by one proc: Mordekaiser's Darkness Rise triggers after he lands three attacks or spells on you, and once it's up his damage aura and move speed turn a close trade into a losing one. Riven's entire job is to land her burst and leave before he reaches three hits, not to stand and slug.

theirWindow.what: He'll look to pull you from 700 range into his Q and auto chain to start stacking the passive. Don't hug minions or stand still in his E range when it's up — if he pulls you, cut the trade short with E (Valor) or Flash rather than fighting out the full exchange.

yourWindow.when: Your Q and W are both off cooldown
yourWindow.what: Open with Q (Broken Wings) to close the gap, stun with W (Ki Burst) at 260 range, and dump empowered Runic Blade autos before he reaches three landed hits. Disengage the instant he hits two — the third is what flips the trade.

start.why: The 91.7% pick rate and 54.5% win rate over 33 games confirm this is the standard start — the extra sustain matters against Obliterate poke while you wait for Death's Grasp to come online.

boots.why: 54.2% win rate over 24 games and the majority pick (68.6%) — the cooldown reduction tightens your Q-W-E all-in loop, which is the only way to win a trade before his third hit lands.

core.why: Every point of damage he deals is magic, and the shield plus spell block covers the burst window right as his Death's Grasp lands.
Your W (Ki Burst) stun applies the CC Eclipse wants, converting your burst window directly into a shield and bonus damage proc.
Sustain through extended trades is what the 10-13 power window is built on — it lets you out-heal his passive aura damage once the fight is already underway.

runes.keystoneWhy: The stacking adaptive force and healing reward exactly the kind of extended, repeated trading this matchup forces once Death's Grasp is online.

summoners.why: 100% pick rate at 55.9% win rate — Flash is your out from a landed Death's Grasp, and Ignite punishes the all-in window before Indestructible can bank enough damage to heal it off.

playing.title: Count his passive hits
playing.detail: Disengage once he's landed two attacks or spells on you. The third grants his damage aura and move speed, and you cannot out-trade that buff mid-fight.

playing.title: Respect Death's Grasp range
playing.detail: It pulls all enemies in a 700-range area. Don't stand still near minion waves when it's off cooldown — getting pulled starts his passive clock for free.

playing.title: Trade when his Q is down
playing.detail: Obliterate's cooldown only drops to 4s at max rank but starts at 8s — early levels, a used Q is your cleanest window to step in with Broken Wings.

playing.title: Save E for his burst, not mobility
playing.detail: Valor blocks incoming damage for its short duration — hold it to eat an Obliterate or auto rather than spending it purely to close distance.

playing.title: Full combo before he shields
playing.detail: Indestructible lets him bank damage into a heal. Land Q-W-E and your empowered autos in one burst window rather than poking, or he just heals the chip damage back.

playing.title: Don't contest his ult 1v1 late
playing.detail: Realm of Death isolates you from your team and steals your stats on a kill. If he's flashed in with R up past level 6, play for your jungler rather than dueling it out alone.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and the 53.3% head-to-head win rate over 30 games are measured from live games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning about Darkness Rise timing and trade windows is my own tactical read, not OP.GG's.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being hit by Mordekaiser’s abilities. Deal burst damage and fall back periodically to prevent Mordekaiser’s (P) from activating.
